Quick Read

IBM's software strength can't offset stalled consulting growth of 2%, leaving the stock down 19% and needing faster services momentum to reclaim $250.

Accenture's 6% revenue growth outpaced IBM's consulting, while Oracle's AI-fueled cash burn drove a 41% slide, a far steeper drop than IBM's.

Bulls cite 22% free cash flow growth, but Arvind Krishna warns transaction processing's double-digit pace will moderate, and January's Q4 report is the test.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

A strong software business hasn't been enough to offset a stalled consulting arm at IBM (NYSE:IBM) this year. IBM stock is down 21% year to date (YTD) to $231.81 in late-day trading. Broad technology selling is adding a 4% decline to that slide.

MajestiX B / Shutterstock.com

Starting 2026 at $288.30, IBM stock spent part of the year above the $250 level. Over the past 52 weeks, IBM has traded between $196.41 and $327.83. Getting back to that round number may take faster consulting growth and continued software momentum at the company.

IBM Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
What Dragged IBM Lower in 2026

The turning point came on July 22, when IBM reported Q2 2026 operating diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.93, missing the $2.97 consensus and ending a five-quarter beat streak. Management cited "revenue headwinds late in the second quarter," and IBM Z mainframe revenue fell 42% as the product cycle aged.

IBM's next report on October 21 told a better story. The company posted its Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.95 against a $2.87 consensus, while its revenue rose 4.7% year over year (YoY) to $17.10 billion. CEO Arvind Krishna said "Transaction processing grew 10%, underscoring the strategic importance of the mainframe and validating our view that the softness we saw in the second quarter reflected timing rather than underlying demand."

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Our look at Why Is Dell Stock Falling Again? found that Dell fell 7.2% on Friday, Nov 13, with no Dell-specific news behind it, as AI stocks slid again. On Monday it fell another 7.0% to $320.55, leaving it 45.5% below its record close of $588.40. The next question is the bigger one: where could the stock be in five years?

Our answer: it depends on one thing, whether Dell's AI-server earnings jump becomes its normal level of profit. If it does, and the stock gets the price-to-earnings multiples it has traded at since the VMware spin-off, the math points to about $595 to $906 a share on fiscal 2030 analyst estimates. These are illustrations, not forecasts. If earnings slip back to fiscal 2026 levels at that year's multiple, the same math gives $114.44.

The surprise is how little of the new earnings the price assumes. At Monday's close Dell traded at 13.2 times its own GAAP earnings guide for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. At the end of each of its last four fiscal years, it traded at between 13.0 and 19.8 times that year's GAAP earnings. So the market is pricing this year's much bigger profit near the lowest multiple of those four years.

Where Dell's Earnings Stand Now

Most readers know the run. Dell closed at $56.70 on Nov 15, 2021; Monday's $320.55 is 465.3% higher. Even after the drop, the stock is up 161.7% from a year ago.

The earnings moved even faster. Dell guided fiscal 2027 GAAP earnings per share of $24.37, 180.8% above fiscal 2026's $8.68. It raised its revenue guide to $192 billion from $167 billion, and its AI-optimized server guide to $74 billion from $60 billion. Behind that sits a record $95 billion AI backlog at the end of July, up from $51.3 billion three months earlier. That backlog is 2.3 times the AI server revenue left in the second half of this year's guide, so a good part of it reaches into next year.

On the past twelve months' earnings, the stock is at 18.6 times, inside its old range. The gap between that and the 13.2 times on this year's guide is the earnings jump the market is not yet paying full price for.

What Would Have To Be True

Analysts' average adjusted estimate for fiscal 2030 (the year to January 2030) is $45.78 a share. Getting there from this year's $25.92 consensus means about 20.9% a year of earnings growth. Here is what Dell's own past multiples, which are based on GAAP earnings, would put on these adjusted estimates, so treat the results as generous:

title: What Needs To Be True To Buy Dell Stock?

What Needs To Be True To Buy Dell Stock?

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Dell Technologies (DELL) stock lost 28.9% in the month to November 16, 2026, while the S&P 500 fell 3.1%. On its September 1 earnings call, management raised its full-year revenue guide by $25 billion, to $192 billion at the midpoint, which is up roughly 70%. The company is guiding to far higher sales, yet its shares are falling. So what does a buyer get for today's price?

Dell Stock's P/E Is Below The S&P 500's

At the November 16 close, Dell traded at 18.6 times its earnings over the past twelve months, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. That lower multiple comes with rising profit: Dell earned $11.4 billion in the four quarters to July 31, 2026, up from $4.84 billion a year earlier.

That profit comes on thin margins. Over the past twelve months, Dell kept 9.6% of its revenue as operating income, compared with 18.9% for the S&P 500. The margin has risen from 6.7% a year earlier, and management said on the September 1 call that scale was the single biggest lever behind the improvement.

What Must Hold For Dell's Profit To Keep Growing?

Dell's AI server orders have to keep turning into sales, and its customers have to keep paying higher prices.

The orders are the best case for owning the stock. Management said Dell ended the quarter to July 31 with a record $95 billion of AI backlog, orders it has not yet delivered. That backlog compares with $16.4 billion of AI server revenue in the same quarter, management said. On the same call, management said demand for Dell's products was exceeding the supply it could get.

The higher prices are the risk. Management said part of the server business's growth comes from price increases as Dell's input costs continue to go up. The company named memory chips as the tightest supply, pointing to DRAM first and NAND after it. Sales won through higher prices last only as long as customers accept them.

Dell's Next Report Comes In November

Dell is scheduled to report its fiscal third quarter of 2027 on November 24, 2026. For that quarter, management guided to revenue of $49 billion at the midpoint, up roughly 80% from a year earlier. Management expects $19 billion of that total from AI servers, and AI server revenue against that guide is the number to watch when Dell reports.

Dell's slide this past month occurred between two quarterly reports. A large position in any one stock is worth an exit plan made before the next swing, not during it.

title: Is Consulting Holding Back IBM Stock?
detail:
Is Consulting Holding Back IBM Stock?
Trefis Team

IBM
NVDA
MSFT
AMZN
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

For shareholders of International Business Machines (IBM), the consulting business is holding back overall growth. Consulting revenue rose 1.8% in fiscal 2025, while the rest of IBM grew 10.2%.

Management said growth accelerated across IBM's segments in the third quarter of 2026. For consulting, it called the change only a modest improvement. If one of those owners sent the consulting team a note this week, it would be short.

IBM Owners Have One Ask For Consulting

The note would begin with what the team means to investors. You brought in 31.2% of IBM's revenue in fiscal 2025, making consulting the company's second-largest business after software.

It would then say that growth is what owners need from you. Management said consulting revenue grew 2% at constant currency in the third quarter of 2026. Clients were modernizing to deploy AI securely and at scale.

Owners would make one ask of you. Management expects consulting revenue growth to pick up modestly this year, to the low-to-mid single digits. It credits the quality of the backlog and momentum in generative AI. Owners want you to deliver that pace. They want you to succeed, because consulting is large enough to set much of the pace for all of IBM.

Where IBM's Consulting Business Is Falling Behind

Consulting's slow pace goes back further. Its revenue fell 0.9% in fiscal 2024, when it made up 33.0% of IBM's revenue. By fiscal 2025 that share had dropped to 31.2%.

In the third quarter of 2026, management said software grew 9% and infrastructure 5%, alongside a modest improvement in consulting. Management also said segment profit margins expanded by 210 basis points in software and 120 basis points in infrastructure.

Consulting went the other direction. Its segment profit margin declined modestly as the team reinvested productivity gains into digital assets. In management's words, this was to speed a move toward a services as software model and capture the growing AI opportunity.

The Case For IBM's Consulting Team

The team has real strengths. Management tied consulting's latest growth to continued client demand for AI-enabled transformation, so clients are still buying the work.

IBM as a whole can also afford the reinvestment. Free cash flow was $14.0 billion over the twelve months ended September 30, 2026, up from $11.9 billion a year earlier. Operating margin over those twelve months was 18.3%, against 17.7% a year before. The company is keeping more of each dollar of sales even as consulting reinvests.

What Triggered Dell Stock's 7% Drop?

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Dell Technologies (DELL) stock fell 7.0% on Monday, November 16, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. The company released no announcements, earnings reports or filings. All 12 other companies in its sub-industry with a market value of $2 billion or more fell the same day. It was Dell's second big drop in two sessions. What was moving tech stocks that day, and what ties Dell to it?

Dell Fell The Day Chip Stocks Slid

Chip stocks fell on November 16. AMD and Intel slid ahead of two big tests for the AI trade that were still to come that day: Nvidia's results on Tuesday and Anthropic's expected trading debut on Thursday. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5% that day.

None of that was Dell news. But AI servers make up a large part of what Dell sells. In fiscal Q2 2027, which ended July 31, 2026, Dell recognized $16.4 billion of AI server revenue. Its total revenue was $47.0 billion. It also ended that quarter with a record $95 billion AI backlog, meaning orders it had taken but not yet delivered.

Did Dell Fall Alone Or With Other Hardware Makers?

Dell fell with its group, but further than most of it. That group is the other companies in technology hardware, storage and peripherals with a market value of $2 billion or more. Their median drop was 5.3%. Six of them fell by 5% or more.

Broader measures fell by less. The technology sector fund XLK fell 3.2%, less than Dell but more than the S&P 500. All five companies on Dell's peer list also fell, each by less than Dell. Hewlett Packard Enterprise dropped 3.6% and HP 2.9%. IBM fell 1.9%, Cisco 1.2% and Apple 1.0%.

Where Does Dell Stock Stand Now?

A fall this large is not rare for Dell. The stock had 12 sessions with a drop at least this large in the prior 365 days. The latest came just one session earlier, on Friday, November 13, when the stock dropped 7.2%.

Over twelve months, Dell stock is still up 141.8%, against 11.4% for the S&P 500. But it closed at $320.55 on November 16. That is well below its highest close of the past year, $588.40 on September 17, 2026. The stock lost 28.9% over the past month alone. At that price, Dell trades at 1.4 times its sales over the last twelve months, against 3.2 times for the S&P 500.

Dell is expected to report its fiscal Q3 2027 results on November 24, 2026. Management expects $19 billion of AI server revenue for that quarter. That is the number to watch.

Dell said nothing new on Monday. It still fell with its whole group, and further than the S&P 500. That is the trouble with owning any one stock. Forces outside the company can move it.
